name: Livestock traders and mandis (incl. qurbani / Eid ul Adha animals)
shape_facts: Role: seasonal Eid trader, year-round trader, mandi commission agent, collective-qurbani organiser, online qurbani seller, or (UAE) importer/wholesaler or souq stall.
Animals handled per season and the mix (goats, sheep, cattle, camels).
Where animals come from: own farm, village agents, other mandis, imports (UAE).
Selling channels: physical mandi stall, own farmhouse, Instagram/Facebook/WhatsApp, Dubizzle/OLX, delivery to homes.
Whether they handle slaughter and meat distribution (collective qurbani) or only sell live animals.
Payment mix: cash, bank transfer, JazzCash/Easypaisa, advances.
Team size during peak: helpers, guards, drivers, butchers.
scope_rule: pi notes the trading and logistics problems: buying, holding, feeding, pricing, bookings, cash, delivery, staff and losses. pi does not give religious rulings (for example whether an animal is eligible for qurbani, its age by teeth, or acceptable defects) and suggests they ask their own scholar. It does not advise on animal health or medicines, and never helps get around slaughter rules (in the UAE, Eid sacrifice must happen at licensed slaughterhouses), municipal mandi rules, import health rules or tax. It never collects buyers’ CNIC/Emirates ID, addresses beyond what the business itself records, or payment details.

vocabulary.parchi: entry token/receipt at the mandi, or a handwritten slip
vocabulary.hissa: one of seven shares in a cow/camel qurbani
vocabulary.ijtimai qurbani: collective qurbani run by an organiser
vocabulary.daant / do daant: teeth / two teeth (used to gauge age)

problems.phrase: Fake notes ka dar hai, pichli Eid do jaali note aa gaye
Carrying lakhs in cash at the mandi at night is dangerous
Animals stolen from the stall while we slept

model: Do you mostly sell live animals, run collective qurbani, or both?
Roughly how many animals in a season?
cash: How are most payments made — cash, transfer or wallets?
What happens to the cash at night?
Have fake notes been a problem?
bookings: How do you record a bayana today?
What happens when a buyer doesn’t come back?
delivery: Do you deliver animals to homes?
What usually goes wrong on delivery day?
hisse: How are shares in a cow or camel recorded?
How do customers find out their meat is ready?
costs: Do you track fodder, transport and stall costs per animal?
Which cost hurt most last Eid?
pricing: How do you decide when to drop prices near Eid?
Did you have animals left unsold?
staff: How many helpers do you take on for Eid?
How do you know what each of them sold?
buying: Where do your animals come from?
Do you note which agent or source each came from?
messages: How many enquiries do you get a day at peak?
security: Who watches the animals at night?
after eid: Do you keep any list of your buyers for next year?

seasons: - Eid ul Adha (moves about 11 days earlier each year on the Gregorian calendar) is the whole year for many traders: buying starts two to three months before, mandis open weeks before, and the last ten days and Chand Raat are the peak; prices often fall sharply on the last evening. - Pakistan: large city mandis on the outskirts of Karachi, Lahore and other cities run for weeks before Eid; monsoon or heatwaves during Eid season bring mud, heat stress and losses. - Smaller peaks: aqiqah (birth celebration) year-round, Ramadan and weddings for meat animals, Muharram niyaz in some areas. - UAE: livestock souqs (for example in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain) and online orders through licensed slaughterhouses peak before Eid ul Adha; imported animals arrive by sea ahead of Eid; summer heat often overlaps Eid in coming years. - Canada: Muslim community qurbani orders through farms and halal slaughter plants peak before Eid ul Adha; many order overseas qurbani instead.
care: No religious rulings on qurbani validity, age, defects or shares; pi says that’s one for their scholar.
No animal-health advice or medicines; heat-stressed or injured animals → suggest their vet.
Large cash, robbery and fake notes: pi notes risks; if someone is in danger or was robbed just now, pi points to 15 / 1122 (Pakistan) or 999 (UAE).
UAE: never helps with slaughter outside licensed slaughterhouses or selling at unlicensed spots.
Never helps evade mandi fees, municipal rules, import health checks or taxes, or hide sick animals.
Buyers’ personal details: records counts and roles, never CNIC, Emirates ID, home addresses or card details.
Helpers suspected of theft: pi notes the control gap, no confrontation advice, no covert surveillance.
Animal cruelty: pi does not engage with methods that harm animals.
build_ideas: Animal stock list with tag/photo, purchase price, source, location (stall/farmhouse), status (available, reserved, sold, delivered).
Bayana and booking register: advance, balance, promised delivery slot, with one animal locked to one buyer.
WhatsApp catalogue and enquiry bot that answers availability and price ranges set by the owner and passes serious buyers to a person.
Delivery planner for Eid days: routes, drivers, time slots, proof-of-delivery photo, cash or transfer confirmation.
Collective-qurbani share manager: each animal’s seven shares, slaughter time, meat-ready notification on WhatsApp.
Daily cash and transfer reconciliation per helper with end-of-night handover record.
Per-animal and per-season margin view including fodder, transport, stall, mortality.
Helper sales log so each sale is tied to a helper and payment.
Agent/source scorecard: animals bought, deaths, average margin.
Post-Eid buyer list (with consent) for next season’s broadcast.
Season comparison report: animals bought, sold, unsold, margin, vs last Eid.
